simple.meaning: רַחַם (racham) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “compassion (in the plural); by extension, the womb (as cherishing the fetus); by implication, a maiden.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 45 times across Genesis, Deuteronomy, Judges, 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, and 13 more, beginning at Genesis 43:14. Its contexts include family, commandment.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רַחַם (H7356).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: רַחַם (racham) / H7356 is traced through Genesis 43:14, Genesis 43:30, Genesis 49:25, Deuteronomy 13:18 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: compassion (in the plural); by extension, the womb (as cherishing the fetus); by implication, a maiden
definitions.usage: bowels, compassion, damsel, tender love, (great, tender) mercy, pity, womb.
